title: 2 Dividend Stocks Built to Hold Up When Markets Don't
author: Adria Cimino
description: The article recommends two Dividend Kings—Johnson & Johnson and AbbVie—as defensive dividend stocks that can provide steady income during market volatility. Both companies have demonstrated consistent dividend growth and strong business fundamentals in their pharmaceutical and healthcare portfolios.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company is praised for its strategic exit from consumer health to focus on high-potential pharma and medtech units. It has 28 products generating over $1 billion annually, eight brands with double-digit growth, and is on track to achieve record revenue exceeding $100 billion. Offers a 1.9% dividend yield with consistent growth history.

Despite losing Humira exclusivity, the company successfully transitioned with newer immunology products Skyrizi and Rinvoq showing ~24% revenue growth. Strong portfolio across aesthetics, neuroscience, and oncology with double-digit growth in several drugs. Worldwide revenue advanced 10% to over $16 billion with a 2.7% dividend yield and long history of dividend increases.

title: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Sees a More Significant Dip Than Broader Market: Some Facts to Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Johnson & Johnson stock declined 2.22% on September 8, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.58% loss. The company is expected to report earnings on October 13, 2026, with forecasted EPS of $2.95 (up 5.36% YoY) and revenue of $25.36 billion (up 5.71% YoY). JNJ holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with a Forward P/E of 23.75, trading at a premium to its industry average.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: JNJ experienced a notable single-day decline of 2.22%, underperforming broader market indices. However, the stock had gained 5.13% prior to this trading day and maintains positive earnings growth forecasts (5.36% EPS growth, 5.71% revenue growth YoY). The Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and premium valuation (Forward P/E of 23.75 vs. industry average of 17.92) suggest a balanced outlook with neither strong bullish nor bearish signals.

title: Is the iShares Pharmaceuticals ETF or iShares Healthcare ETF the Better Fund for 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: The article compares two healthcare-focused ETFs from iShares: IHE (Pharmaceuticals ETF) with 55 holdings and IYH (Healthcare ETF) with 100 holdings. While IHE delivered stronger 1-year returns of 50% versus IYH's 27.4%, the article recommends IYH as the better choice due to superior 3- and 5-year performance, greater diversification, and larger asset base of $3.9B. Both funds have identical 0.37% expense ratios.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong recent 1-year performance (50% return) but underperformed on 3-, 5-, and 10-year returns. More concentrated portfolio with higher risk profile (lower beta of 0.49 indicates less volatility but narrower focus). Not recommended as the better choice despite recent gains.

Recommended as the better fund choice due to superior 3-year (19.9% vs 10%) and 5-year (11.9% vs 5.5%) annualized returns. Offers broader diversification with 100 holdings, larger AUM of $3.9B providing better liquidity, and more balanced exposure across healthcare subsectors.

title: Ulcerative Colitis Market Outlook: 5 Late-Stage Drug Candidates to Watch | DelveInsight
author: Delveinsight
description: The ulcerative colitis market is experiencing significant growth with emerging therapies addressing unmet needs in moderate-to-severe disease. The market, valued at approximately USD 9.4 billion in 2025, is projected to expand at a CAGR of 7.6% through 2036. Five promising late-stage candidates—Obefazimod (Abivax), Tulisokibart (Merck), Afimkibart (Roche), Icotrokinra (J&J/Protagonist), and Duvakitug (Teva/Sanofi)—are reshaping the treatment landscape with novel mechanisms targeting IL-23 and TL1A pathways, while established biologics and oral therapies continue to maintain market presence.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Obefazimod demonstrated positive Phase III results with rapid symptom improvements and favorable safety profile comparable to placebo, positioning it as a first-in-class miR-124 enhancer with significant market potential.

Tulisokibart met primary endpoints in Phase 3 ATLAS-UC trial, demonstrating clinical remission superiority over placebo with consistent safety profile, strengthening Merck's position in the growing UC market.
Afimkibart showed strong Phase IIb efficacy (35% remission vs 12% placebo) and is advancing to Phase III trials with regulatory filing anticipated in 2027, supporting Roche's IBD portfolio expansion.

Icotrokinra demonstrated sustained clinical benefits across multiple endpoints in Phase 2b trials and has advanced to Phase 3 ICONIC-UC program, offering a novel once-daily oral IL-23 receptor antagonist with broad applicability.

Duvakitug secured $400 million strategic funding from Blackstone Life Sciences for continued development, indicating strong confidence in the TL1A inhibitor's potential in Phase III trials for UC and Crohn's disease.
Co-developed Icotrokinra with J&J, a first-in-class oral IL-23 receptor antagonist showing strong clinical efficacy, positioning the company as an innovator in oral peptide therapeutics for IBD.
Co-developing Duvakitug with Teva and eligible for milestone payments and royalties, providing exposure to a promising TL1A-targeting therapy in the expanding IBD market.

title: Lilly vs. J&J: Betting on Breakout Growth or Built-In Stability?
author: Na
description: Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson are compared as investment opportunities in the healthcare sector. Lilly is driven by its dominant GLP-1 franchise (Mounjaro, Zepbound) generating $27.6B in H1 2026 sales, with new oral therapy Foundayo and pipeline candidate Retatrutide offering future growth. J&J offers diversification across pharmaceuticals and medical devices with 28 products generating over $1B annually, steady 6.2% organic growth in Innovative Medicines, and 64 consecutive years of dividend increases. While J&J shows better valuation and recent stock performance (+33% YTD), Lilly is selected as the superior long-term pick due to substantially stronger earnings-growth prospects, despite facing pricing pressures and GLP-1 market competition.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong growth momentum in cardiometabolic franchise with blockbuster GLP-1 drugs generating $27.6B in H1 2026. New oral therapy Foundayo offers competitive advantage. Late-stage pipeline candidate Retatrutide has multibillion-dollar potential. Diversifying portfolio through M&A and new product launches. Selected as better long-term investment despite higher valuation (26.87 P/E) due to substantially stronger earnings-growth prospects (48.4% EPS growth expected in 2026).

Diversified business model with 28 products generating over $1B annually reduces risk. Innovative Medicines segment growing 6.2% organically despite Stelara patent cliff. Strong cash generation and 64 consecutive years of dividend increases (2% yield). Better valuation (22.16 P/E) and stronger recent stock performance (+33% YTD). However, faces headwinds from patent cliffs and MedTech softness, resulting in lower earnings growth expectations (7.4% in 2026).
